- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 15–30% for next 30-day horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% to account for risk reversal or market panic.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 20–40% for 2–3 days post-spike.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.33 → -0.33 → +0.33), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently near zero (≤ 0.10) despite high sentiment, model is overconfident; apply “sentiment-to-price” scaling: multiply forecast by 0.3–0.5 if sentiment > 0.67 and outcome < 0.10.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.33), model often fails to capture volatility; use sentiment variance as multiplier: if sentiment std > 0.2, scale forecast down 10–20%.
